key_insight: Eu²⁺/Eu³⁺ redox chemistry pins the Fermi level, overcoming self-limiting nitrogen incorporation in titanate-derived perovskite oxynitrides.
engineering_relevance: Fermi-level engineering offers a route to control oxynitride composition during synthesis, although the abstract does not demonstrate solar-cell performance or an AI method.
method: Combine theoretical defect modelling with experimental characterisation.
Tune A-site composition in Eu–Ba and Eu–Ca titanate-derived oxynitrides.
Use Eu²⁺/Eu³⁺ charge compensation to sustain nitrogen substitution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports nitrogen uptake limited to 0.03 per formula unit in barium titanate-derived material versus up to 0.65 with Eu-based compensation, measured by hot gas extraction, and Fermi-level pinning near 2.9 eV above the valence-band maximum.
watch_item: Further nitrogen incorporation remains limited by bond-angle distortion within Ti(O,N)₆ octahedra.
paper_title: Controlling nitrogen incorporation in (Eu,Ba,Ca)TiO$_3$-derived perovskite-type oxynitrides through Fermi Level Engineering
